Maybe I read through this too quickly as its supposed to be one of the longer chapters.
I think this chapter has some of the best strengths but also greatest flaws so far. The construction of Satokos character is amazing in this, and is definitely more emotionally provoking in making you actually care what happens.
The atmosphere that is built up is very strong, coalescing as usual around the Watanagashi festival. The slice of life segments prior also felt fairly refreshing. The moment when Keiichi is doing his crime in the rain is incredible. Very engaging and dark and just completely engrossing in atmosphere. It felt like a true fruition of the concept of a 'Sound Novel'. 
So yeah, without going too much into it this was a very dark chapter, I liked how it felt very respectful in this sense. Part of what didn't thrill me about the endings of CH-1 and CH-2 is they felt so over the top I dont know if there was a hint of comedy in it. Obviously due to the profound subject nature of CH-3 covering child abuse, yeah Im glad it didn't feel as over the top. It felt grounded. I wouldn't say depressing, as CH-2 was the saddest out of the chapters so far, It moreso feels just incredibly scary and real. profound. But not in the way of CH-1s horror.

But the ending, is still quite eh. I understand the direction its trying to go in, and its trying to confuse you the reader as much as possible. But this was just such a jump from both CH-1 and CH-2 its insane. It basically solves every answer but leaves you with about 20 more which again is fine and all but it feels quite overloaded and backheavy. It lulls you into the story thinking this is going to be more focused on satoko, which it is, but then just dumps so much ♥♥♥♥ in the back half you have no way to even comprehend what you just read. Its peak, but part of me thinks there could of been a degree of separation in this regard. It just felt like a lot of the conspiratorial stuff at the end was just so much not needed, and a lot of it shouldve just been said rather than described. or left to one of the answer arcs. I really dont get why anything past the final incident was included but who knows. It really makes me feel conflicted because other than that this chapter was a solid 9, 9.5/10, but with all this included its more like a 7 or 8. Still really good, but just so backheavy.

I get the narrative beats the story is going for at this point, I think I know relatively whats going on but who knows.  This review probably wont be read by anyone or help anyone i dont know if i can call it a review even, but if youre already this far in I guess theres no point to just keep on going. I have no clue how this will resolve itself plot wise but thematically its pretty obvious since the ending of ch1.

En primer lugar, me desdigo de algo que dije en la reseña del capítulo previo: No compres/jueges este episodio de Higurashi sin antes pasar por los dos previos. Y si el primero (que es gratuito) no te gusto, no te molestes en seguir, esto va a ser más de los mismo en trama y jugabilidad.
Ya en este párrafo supongo que quedan los fieles, y en ese sentido puede ser una tarea innecesaria reseñar un juego para gente que ya esta enganchado a la saga. Pero me parece clave explicar porque ya en este juego seguir el orden es vital. A diferencia de los capítulos 1 y 2, que pueden funcionar fácilmente sin leer el otro, en el capítulo 3 el trasfondo acumulado en los otros capítulos es importante para ubicarse y entender a los personajes. Amén de que se captan mejor los guiño que hace el juego, se empieza a no entender un pito de cosas que pasan, ya no de fondo sino en primera línea... Arrancar la saga acá es  cerrar los ojos a buena parte del material puesto adrede por los desarrolladores. Dicho esto, paso a reseñar el juego...
En primer lugar, la trama de este episodio es dura, pero bien DURA. El foco esta en la relación entre Keishi y Satoko, en como es perturbada por la irrupción de personajes externos y lo que pasara con relación a eso. Pero de fondo siguen girando las piezas de relojería de la trama principal: La maldición de Oyashiro-sama, la fiesta de watanagashi y el precio del petróleo. Por la propia dureza de lo que pasa y la ausencia de una traducción  oficial o extraoficial (tema presente en toda la saga), se me hizo muy cuesta arriba, empezandolo en enero de 2024 y terminandolo recién ahora; la duración real del juego debe estar en el entorno de las 10-12 horas, siempre que no te pegue la melancolía y te pongas con otra cosa sin cerrarlo antes (mi caso).
Si hablamos de los puntos fuertes, la historia es el principal (recuerden que no hay jugabilidad en clave "elije esto o aquello", como pasa con las novelas visuales standar) y el apartado sonoro. El juego aborda con responsabilidad y realismo "el viaje" de Kenshi hacia... la locura? el crimen? madurar?, poniendote en los pantalones de un joven adolescente que se siente obligado a crecer para arreglar el mundo.  Y lo que le pasa le da algunas lecciones; si la pensamos en clave historia moralizante, el mensaje bastante claro es que no existen las soluciones fáciles, las acciones tienen consecuencias impredecibles, y hay que vivir (y sobrevivir) con ellas.
Retomando lo sonoro, es un capítulo donde incluso al ominoso chirriar de las cigarras se lo recibe con gusto, por el ambiente opresivo y la gradual desaparición (temprana en el juego) de escapes cómicos o momentos felices: El sonido remacha que los personajes la pasan como el tujes y que nos toca acompañarlos en el sufrimiento.
Con relación a la "gran historia" de fondo en el juego, este episodio ya comienza a dejar entrever más claramente hilos de la trama; aún no los principales, pero si alguno que permiten intuir/sospechar por donde van los tiros y que o quienes no están donde deberían estar en esta historia.

If Onikakushi scares the ♥♥♥♥ out of me, while Watanagashi made me cry, then Tatarigoroshi made me feel both. 

[b][i]NOT A SPOILER-FREE REVIEW[/i][/b]

[spoiler]In all seriousness, I actually expected to get scared like how the first two chapters have been doing (have a “joyful” character who actually turned out to be crazy), which Rena and Mion successfully managed to do to me. However, Tatarigoroshi surprised me with something else. Personally, what made this chapter truly scary in a psychological sense is Satoko’s hopeless abuse situation. When the friend group repeatedly says that there’s nothing they could do, I just felt so awful. Finding out that Satoko has been abused for pretty much her whole life and only getting a temporary sense of relief until her uncle came back is disheartening. And let's not get started on how she has been blaming herself this whole time for her Nii-nii’s disappearance because she thought she was a burden :((. The fact that before knowing about Satoko’s situation, you’d just see her as an annoying but a happy brat who pranks anyone, until she isn't. In Tatarigoroshi, Ryukishi did a great job of showing that she is more than that— she’s a helpless victim of abuse who’s trying her very best to keep up her cheerful appearance. Seeing this shatter during the part where she started screaming and throwing chairs in the classroom broke my heart. This happened all because Keiichi patted Satoko and probably gave her PTSD… my poor baby 😭.[/spoiler] 

[spoiler]What happened next was another moment that gave me goosebumps. It was when Keiichi realized that the only way he could save Satoko was to kill her uncle. Seeing him transform into a desperate “friend” who resorted to killing shows just how hopeless Satoko’s situation was. To add salt to the wound, Ryukishi decided not to kill off Satoko’s uncle for a reason, making the audience dumbfounded. We all saw Keiichi murder Satoko’s uncle, so why did it not happen? This soon drives Keiichi into a series of events that eventually lead to madness. When Satoko’s uncle finally did die, the price was the lives of everyone in Hinamizawa. Keiichi finally got the very thing that he wanted in the first place, but at what cost? It doesn't matter anymore now that his friends, family, and almost everyone in Hinamizawa are dead. And again, realizing just how HOPELESS this situation was and how there was NOTHING you could do but watch will ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crush you.[/spoiler]
